N.E.W.S. investigative feature examining neighborhood redevelopment, gentrification, and the changing character of historically Black communities, I would like to hear from longtime, lifelong, and generational residents, former residents, and business owners of Atlanta's Old Fourth Ward. ⠀ WHAT ARE YOUR THOUGHTS ABOUT THE CHANGES THAT HAVE TAKEN PLACE OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES? ⠀ Has redevelopment improved the neighborhood and created new opportunities? Has it made the community increasingly unaffordable for longtime residents and their families? Have you or your family been priced out of the neighborhood? Were you forced to sell your home, relocate, or close your business because of rising rents, property taxes, or other development pressures? ⠀ Or do you believe the Old Fourth Ward has lost some of the historical and cultural character that made it such a special community? ⠀ Perhaps you believe it's a combination of these experiences. ⠀ I'm interested in hearing your stories, memories, and experiences, whether you still live in the Old Fourth Ward, have since moved away, or once operated a business there. ⠀ Everybody has a story to tell. The A.T.L. wants to know yours. ⠀ If you have a connection to Atlanta's Old Fourth Ward and would like to share your experiences for this upcoming investigation, please reach out to me through a direct message. ⠀ #OldFourthWard #DowntownAtlanta #AtlantaHistory #TheMasquerade #StudioPlex #HistoricDistrictDevelopmentCorporation #HDDC #NoNamesDesigns #TheRoyalPeacock #TheBeautifuls #MurderKroger #AtlantaCityHallEastBuilding #EbenezerBaptistChurch #BigBethelAME #WheatStreetBaptist #WheatStreetTowers #HaugabrooksFuneralHome #KrispyKreme #OldSpaghettiFactory #MangosCaribbeanRestaurant #AtlantaBeltLine #Gentrification #CommunityVoices #ATLNEWS

small-business-owners-in-india-lost-deal.headline: Small Business Owners in India - Lost Deals From Unclear Websites
small-business-owners-in-india-lost-deal.author: Ravi Rai
small-business-owners-in-india-lost-deal.core: Posted in last 7 days Small Business Owners in India - Lost Deals From Unclear Websites The message came in at 9.40 on a Tuesday night. Four words and a full stop. "Sir, they went ahead." ₹6.2 lakh. Three calls, a scoped proposal, a demo of software we already run in production. Lost to a company whose product I know is worse than ours. I said thank you, wished them well, closed the laptop. Then I sat in the dark for forty minutes going over every call in my head looking for the sentence where I lost it. There was no sentence. The next morning I opened the winner's website properly for the first time, with a notebook, not to admire it. Nine minutes. Their site answered the three questions a buyer asks before they trust anybody. Ours answered them on page four. That was the whole difference. Not the product. Not the price. The reading order. Here is the part that took me years to accept: your buyer cannot judge your work. A patient cannot judge a surgeon from the waiting room. So they judge what they can judge, and all of it is on your website. 1. Can I tell in five seconds what you do and who for 2. Is there proof a real person got a real result 3. Can I reach a human without a form that asks my budget A worse business with a clearer website wins almost every time, and it wins quietly, without you ever finding out why. So I wrote down the teardown I have run about sixty times for clients. Twenty minutes, free tools, no account anywhere: → The five-second test on your phone, both sites → The three questions, counted in screens → pagespeed.web.dev on mobile, reading LCP and CLS, not the score everyone argues about → A site: search, which prints a rival's whole keyword strategy in public for free → Trust signals counted, not sensed → Taps from homepage to a filled enquiry, theirs against yours Then a 24-point scorecard you fill in for both sites, and you act on the three lines where they beat you by two. Not all 24. Three. Free fixes first, because they move enquiries most: your first screen, a phone number on every page, a WhatsApp link, asking every customer for a Google review, replying the same working day. The article has the scorecard to paste into a notes app, the rupee cost of each fix, and the written message to send your developer. That last one matters: most teardowns die on a phone call where the developer says "yes yes, we will see" and nothing was written down. Save this one. You will want it the next time you lose one you should have won. And the real question, which is why I published the embarrassing part: have you ever lost work you were certain of and only found out why months later? What did it turn out to be? Tell me below. I read every one and the good ones go into the article with your name on them. If you would rather not say it in public, message me. Send me your site and your competitor's and I will run the same 24 points on both and send you the filled sheet. No charge. #smallbusiness #marketing #india #entrepreneurship

former-corporate-employees-reinvention-a.headline: Former Corporate Employees - Reinvention After Layoff & Career Change
former-corporate-employees-reinvention-a.author: Christine Dolan
former-corporate-employees-reinvention-a.core: Posted in last 7 days Former Corporate Employees - Reinvention After Layoff & Career Change Well, this wasn't exactly on my five-year plan. On May 7th, after more than 20 years in corporate America, I learned my position was being eliminated. And something unexpected happened. For the first time in a long time, I had the space to ask myself: What the hell do I actually want? Not what I'm qualified to do. Not what looks impressive on LinkedIn. Not what everyone else thinks I should be doing. What do I actually want? After spending decades trying to fit into roles, environments, and expectations that didn't always fit me, I realized something. Maybe I didn't need to get better at fitting in. Maybe I needed to stop trying so damn hard. So, after 10 years of wanting to start my own business but having absolutely no idea what that business should be, I'm officially introducing: MY MISFIT LIFE. A coaching business, podcast, and growing community for people ready to stop living according to expectations that no longer fit. Because you can be incredibly successful at building a life you don't actually want. And you can be really fucking good at something that makes you miserable. SO, WHAT AM I BUILDING? COACHING I'm working with people navigating life's transitions. Layoffs, career changes, burnout, relationships, reinvention, or simply reaching that point where you wonder, Is this really it? Through my Misfit Method, we'll question assumptions, explore possibilities, and figure out what actually fits your life now. No cookie-cutter advice. No pretending there's one right way to live. THE MY MISFIT LIFE PODCAST Honest, funny, sometimes uncomfortable conversations about the human experience. And I'm officially looking for guests! Experts, authors, researchers, coaches, and professionals with interesting perspectives? Absolutely. Everyday people who've started over, challenged expectations, or learned something worth sharing? Hell yes. You don't need an impressive title or thousands of followers. Just something interesting to say. A GROWING COMMUNITY I'm creating resources and connections for people who are tired of feeling like they have to become someone else to belong. HERE'S MY ASK: Interested in coaching? Email [email redacted] with the subject Coaching Inquiry. Want to be a podcast guest? Email [email redacted] with the subject Podcast Guest and tell me a little about yourself and what you'd love to discuss. And, if someone comes to mind for either, please share or tag them! My website is still under construction, but I'm not waiting for everything to be perfectly packaged to get started. I spent a lot of years trying to figure out where I fit. Now I'm building something around the idea that maybe we don't have to. Welcome to My Misfit Life. #MyMisfitLife #LifeCoaching #PodcastGuests #Reinvention

travel-couple-and-india-podcast-creators.core: Posted in last 7 days Travel, Couple & India Podcast Creators - Earnings, Growth, Challenges I’m working on four stories for The Creators Index, a platform covering the creator economy, and I’m looking to speak with creators and industry professionals who can share their experiences and insights. I’m particularly interested in connecting with people working in the following areas: 1. Travel Creators: Travel creators who can speak about the ins and outs of travel content creation as well as tourism boards and travel creator programs such as those by the Expedia Group, Headout, Stayvista, etc. 2. Couple Creators: Couple creators who can share insights into audience engagement, what is appealing about couple reels, and the financial realities of couple content creation. 3. Podcasting in India: Podcast hosts, producers, editors, and creators who have launched, grown, or discontinued shows. I’m keen to understand production economics, audience retention, monetisation, and the challenges of sustaining a podcast. 4. Is It Too Late to Become a Creator in 2026? Creators at different stages of their journeys, from established names to those who started recently, as well as people who have struggled to grow despite consistent efforts. I’d love to understand how the barriers to entry, growth opportunities, and monetisation have changed. I’m especially keen to hear first-hand experiences, real numbers where people are comfortable sharing them, and insights beyond the usual success stories. If you work in any of these areas or can connect me with relevant people, please comment below or DM me. I’d love to connect for a potential interview. Please feel free to share this post with anyone who might be a good fit. Thank you! #Journalism #CreatorEconomy #ContentCreators #Podcasting #TravelInfluencers #JournoRequest The Creators Index

natural-birth-midwife-fluent-english-pod.headline: Natural Birth Midwife Fluent English - Podcast Guest Birth Trauma
natural-birth-midwife-fluent-english-pod.author: Ari Kärkkäinen
natural-birth-midwife-fluent-english-pod.core: Posted in last 7 days Natural Birth Midwife Fluent English - Podcast Guest Birth Trauma "Anyone in the world who is clamping and cutting newborn babies' umbilical cords quickly should go to prison" That's from Ibu Robin Lim, a natural birth midwife. Last Friday, I asked a Spanish midwife (also experienced with natural births) what percentage of women give natural birth in Spain, and her response freaked me out a bit. She said a hospital might have about 3 natural births a year! Only three. According to Ibu, many of us carry traumas for decades from our birth. It's all become so clinical; the whole experience is portrayed as scary, and we've disconnected. Why am I posting this? I would love to speak with a natural birth midwife on my podcast. Do you know one? One with an open heart and fluent English. The show is about what we leave behind when we die, and it'd be valuable to speak with someone who's seen many of us arrive. I'll try to reach out to Ibu too, but no idea how. To add to the topic, crazy things I've heard: - Women are increasingly asking the labor to be induced weeks before the due date - Placenta is valued at around $17,000 USD - Birth center nurses often aren't aware of vaginal seeding for cesarean-born babies The original sin of our species might well be its separation from nature. What else should I know about this topic? 🔆

firsttime-founders-lessons-nobody-warned.author: nexushaus
firsttime-founders-lessons-nobody-warned.core: Posted in last 7 days First-Time Founders - Lessons Nobody Warned You About Title: What's something about building your first business that nobody warned you about? I've been spending time talking to early-stage founders lately, and one thing I've noticed is that everyone's journey looks different. Some people struggle to get their first customer. Others struggle with cash flow, finding the right people, getting distribution, or simply figuring out what to focus on next. I'm working on Founder Files, a YouTube interview series where I want to have honest conversations with founders about what building a business actually looks like the decisions, mistakes, setbacks, and lessons that usually don't make it into success stories. I'm also building NexusHaus, a community focused on connecting founders and helping them learn from one another. I'm particularly keen to hear from first-time founders and people in the early stages of building something. It doesn't have to be a tech startup a manufacturing business, service company, local brand, or any other venture is equally worth talking about. I'd love to hear from you: What's been the hardest part of building your business so far? What's one thing you wish you'd known before starting? What's a lesson you learned the hard way? And if you're building something and would be open to sharing your journey on Founder Files, feel free to mention what you're working on in the comments. I'd genuinely like to hear your stories.
